model_or_family: Sky Hawk - Fuzz and Treble Booster
evidence_summary: Tone Machines states the Conrad Sky Hawk was among the Conrad effects built by Applied Audio. The 1969 and 1970 catalogs both list the Sky Hawk, although surviving specimens are not currently documented in the research pass.
Tone Machines identifies the Conrad Bass Hawk as one of the Conrad effects built by Applied Audio. Effects Database separately identifies the Bass Hawk within the Applied Big Bass family.

physical_builder_candidate: Applied Audio Products, Inc. / Sano relationship unresolved
evidence_summary: Tone Machines states the June 1968 factory report confirmed Applied Audio was already working with Sano and building amplifiers and effects. A separate 2024 Effects Database entry confirms the Sano Fuzz and Treble Booster as a distinct cataloged product. Because period model-level factory documentation is not yet in hand, the physical-builder field remains qualified.

A 1968 Goya catalog describes the Boom Box as a USA-made battery-operated transistor bass unit. Tone Machines places the 1968 Goya Boom Box in the Applied lineup and identifies post-1966 Goya effects as Applied-made.

Tone Machines states Goya added the Fury Box to its lineup in 1968 and identifies Goya post-1966 effects as made by Applied Audio. Effects Database places Conrad Fuzzy Fury and Goya Fury Box in the Applied Big Fuzz family.
Tone Machines states Goya added the Power Box in 1969 and describes it as an early LPB-1 copy within the Applied Goya lineup. Post-1966 Goya effects are identified there as Applied-made.

A June 1968 factory report summarized by Tone Machines states that Applied Audio was already working with Sano, building Sano amplifiers and effects. This supports a direct Applied-Sano manufacturing relationship at the company level, while individual model attribution remains subject to model-specific evidence.
